mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25 percentage points, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05) during the specified trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) of at least 2,000 suggests labor market strengthening, which is associated with higher S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investor confidence improves.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward returns do not exceed the average of the prior 12 months (mean difference < 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds 2% above its 12-month average, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are predicted to be positive as demand growth supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10) relative to the pre-trigger 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 3% indicates supply-side weakness, which should produce negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as market anticipates slower growth.
failure_condition: Over 10 consecutive triggered periods, the 5-day forward returns average positive (mean > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages create a conflicting signal, but the interaction of rising rates and higher unemployment is expected to drive negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > FEDFUNDS MA(12m) AND UNRATE > UNRATE MA(12m)
regime_hint: co-occurrence of rate hike and job market weakening
failure_condition: The interaction effect (IC) is not significant (p > 0.05) in the walk-forward test across 24 months.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months, it signals improving labor market conditions and supports higher S&P 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate stronger hiring.
regime_hint: labor market softening turning to strength
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain flat or decline over the next 6 months despite the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in HOUST (housing starts) by at least 10% above the prior quarter's average is associated with positive S&P 60-day forward returns as it signals economic momentum and optimism.
failure_condition: Over 12 months post-trigger, 60-day forward returns do not outperform the S&P's 12-month average (mean difference ≤ 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS (retail sales) falls below 95% of its 12-month average, S&P 20-day forward returns are expected to turn negative due to weak consumer demand and supply chain compression.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of such triggered periods over a 2-year horizon.
